Synopsis:
Jergal, a god of the dead, awaits the player in camp. He is bound by the judgment of another god - Helm - to assist the players as penance for past crimes. He provides resurrection services to the players.

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_Jergal.json: Jergal appears in camp in the guise of Withers, a talking skeleton bound by Helm’s judgment to atone for past crimes by aiding the party with matters of death. He spends his time poring over scrolls and muttering, and will bluntly offer to reattach soul to body — i.e., resurrect fallen companions — for a price. Beyond straight resurrection, he can provide related services (summoning or aid from dead spirits, and the game’s respecialization/class‑change options) in exchange for coin. Other camp NPCs (e.g., Volo) or the wider city events (Orin/Gortash/Bhaal‑related crises) may be happening off‑screen, but they don’t change his basic role as the party’s paid resurrection/afterlife contact.
- CHA_Crypt_JergalWandering.json: death--Jergal--climbs out of his sarcophagus to greet them. He has been locked inside for years by the god Helm to atone for his part in raising the Dead Three, wicked gods who are now plotting to conquer the realms. Jergal is emotionless and excessively formal, both resigned to his fate and that of others. He is here to assist the party because that is his divine oath, not out of any true desire to act. Players can attempt to goad or attack him, but to minimal effect, as he is functionally immortal. His only goal was to see their faces, so he can find them at camp later to offer further assistance.
- CHA_Crypt_Jergal.json: After the party has slain a group of undead scholars, the judge of death--Jergal--climbs out of his sarcophagus to greet them. He has been locked inside for years by the god Helm to atone for his part in raising the Dead Three, wicked gods who are now plotting to conquer the realms. Jergal is emotionless and excessively formal, both resigned to his fate and that of others. He is here to assist the party because that is his divine oath, not out of any true desire to act. Players can attempt to goad or attack him, but to minimal effect, as he is functionally immortal. His only goal was to see their faces, so he can find them at camp later to offer further assistance.
- CAMP_Jergal_AD_PlayerResurrection.json: Jergal resurrects one or multiple players at the camp.
- SCL_Drider_Caravan_HalfOrcCaster.json: Player approaches Kansif (a stoic, honourable male half-orc) and Brawler Vez (a mouthy female goblin) after clearing a checkpoint and entering their camp in the Shadowcurse. They two Absolute cultists assume you're a True Soul sent by Minthara (which may or may not be true) and will ask if you brought the lyre needed to summon their guide through the darkness. If you have, you can play it and the drider will emerge. If you haven't, they can tell you where to find it.

context: Jergal appears in camp as Withers, a talking, emotionless skeleton and the judge of the dead who was locked by the god Helm to atone for past crimes and bound to assist the party. He pores over scrolls and will bluntly offer to reattach soul to body (resurrection), summon or call on dead spirits, or provide respecialization/class‑change services—for a price. His help is given because of his divine oath, not out of sympathy, and he is functionally immortal and scarcely swayed by taunts or threats. Other NPCs and off‑screen city events may be happening, but they do not change his basic role as the camp’s paid contact for matters of death.
